'''Terrell Eldorado Owens''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|t|ɛr|əl}}; born December 7, 1973) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] [[wide receiver]] who played 15 seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). Also known by his initials "'''T.O.'''", Owens ranks third in NFL career receiving yards and receiving touchdowns. Owens played [[college football]] for the [[Chattanooga Mocs football|Chattanooga Mocs]] and was selected in the third round of the [[1996 NFL draft]] by the [[San Francisco 49ers]]. He was a member of the team for seven seasons until he was traded to the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] in 2004. Two years later, he signed with the [[Dallas Cowboys]], where he spent three seasons. Owens' NFL career concluded after one season each with the [[Buffalo Bills]] and [[Cincinnati Bengals]]. He later played for the [[Allen Wranglers]] of the [[Indoor Football League]] (IFL) in 2012 and last played professionally with [[Fan Controlled Football]] (FCF) in 2022.<ref name=signswithfcf>{{Cite web |last=Kerr |first=Jeff |date=March 31, 2022 |title=Terrell Owens coming out of retirement to play in Fan Controlled Football League, per report |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/terrell-owens-coming-out-of-retirement-to-play-in-fan-controlled-football-league-per-report/ |access-date=April 2, 2022 |website=[[CBSSports.com]] |language=en}}</ref>

A six-time [[Pro Bowl]] and five-time first-team [[All-Pro]] selection, Owens also created a significant amount of controversy during his professional career and attracted attention for his flamboyant [[touchdown celebration]]s. He was inducted into the [[Pro Football Hall of Fame]] in 2018.

Despite his short seven-year career (with four full seasons), Davis is often regarded as one of the greatest running backs of all time.{{cite web | url=https://www.nfl.com/photos/gil-brandt-s-25-greatest-nfl-running-backs-of-all-time-0ap3000000815786 | title=Gil Brandt's 25 greatest NFL running backs of all time | website=[[NFL.com]]}} Davis was selected by the Broncos in the sixth round (196th pick overall) of the [[1995 NFL draft]]. Davis still holds the NFL record for most rushing touchdowns in a single postseason, scoring eight in the [[1997–98 NFL playoffs|1997 playoffs]], culminating in him winning the Super Bowl MVP award.{{Cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/leaders/rush_td_single_season_playoffs.htm|title=NFL Rushing Touchdowns Single-Season Playoffs Leaders|website=Pro-Football-Reference.com|access-date=July 4, 2019}} In 1998, he became only the fourth NFL player to [[2,000-yard club|rush for over 2,000 yards in a season]]. Davis is also credited with starting the "Mile High Salute", a celebratory tradition among Denver Broncos players after scoring a touchdown. He was elected into the [[Pro Football Hall of Fame]] in 2017.

Terrence founded an independent start-up real estate brokerage named [https://www.tm5collegestation.com/ TM5 Team] and has brokered $2 Billion + in sales volume and has been involved in over 8,000 real estate transactions. TM5 merged with eXp Realty in 2021, where Terrence is a 3X ICON agent and his organization completed over $1.269B in total sales in 2023.

Terrence is a founder or investor in over 70+ companies under the [https://terrencemurphy.com/companies/ Terrence Murphy Companies] brand and has now moved into professional sports ownership. He is a real estate developer and home builder whose company [https://murphysignaturehomes.com/ Murphy Signature Homes] recently won the [https://www.inc.com/profile/murphy-signature-homes Inc. 5000 award] for one of America's fastest growing private owned companies. Terrence is on the board of [[Alumni Ventures]], Texas A&M’s VC fund [https://www.av.vc/funds/ring Ring Ventures].

'''Terrell Raymonn Suggs''' (born October 11, 1982), nicknamed "'''T-Sizzle'''", is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] for 17 seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Arizona State Sun Devils football|Arizona State Sun Devils]], and was recognized as a [[unanimous All-American]]. He was selected by the [[Baltimore Ravens]] with the 10th overall pick in the [[2003 NFL draft]], and is the franchise's all-time leader in [[quarterback sack|sacks]].<ref name="RavensCareerDefense" /> He also played for the [[Arizona Cardinals]] and the [[Kansas City Chiefs]].

Suggs is a seven-time [[Pro Bowl]] selection, a two time [[All-Pro]], and was named [[NFL Defensive Player of the Year]] in 2011. Suggs won two Super Bowls in his career, [[Super Bowl XLVII]] in [[2012 Baltimore Ravens season|2012]] with the Ravens and [[Super Bowl LIV]] in [[2019 Kansas City Chiefs season|2019]] with the Chiefs. '''Terrell Antoine Fletcher''' (born September 14, 1973) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who spent his entire eight-year career as a [[running back]] for the [[San Diego Chargers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). In 1995, Fletcher was named MVP in the Hall of Fame [[Outback Bowl]]. With the Chargers, he rushed for 1,871 yards and gained 1,943 yards receiving,<ref>[http://www.nfl.com/players/profile?id=FLE726755 NFL Stats].{{Retrieved | accessdate=December 29, 2010}}</ref> leading all Charger running backs in receptions for five consecutive seasons, from 1996 to 2000.<ref name=":0" /> He is the older brother of former [[Indianapolis Colts]] [[tight end]] [[Bryan Fletcher (tight end)|Bryan Fletcher]].<ref>[http://www.colts.com/sub.cfm?page=bio&player_id=325 Bryan Fletcher Profile] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080612041814/http://www.colts.com/sub.cfm?page=bio&player_id=325 |date=2008-06-12 }}.{{Retrieved | accessdate=December 29, 2010}}</ref> On November 4, 2001, he caught [[Drew Brees]]'s first completion.

Fletcher graduated from [[Hazelwood East High School]] in [[Hazelwood, Missouri]] in 1991. He is a first-generation college graduate. He graduated from the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]] with a bachelor's degree in English Literature (1998). In 2003, Fletcher graduated with a master's degree in Religious Studies, from [https://www.socalsem.edu/ Southern California Seminary]. He is also has a Doctorate of Transformational Leadership from [[Bakke Graduate University]] (2018).

Fletcher is currently an ordained Bishop and Senior Pastor for City of Hope International Church in San Diego, California <ref name=":1" /> and married to Kavalya Fletcher (formerly Kavalya Young).

'''Terrelle Pryor Sr.'''<ref>{{Cite web |last=Byrnes |first=D.J. |date=September 6, 2016 |title=Cleveland Browns Name Terrelle Pryor Starting Wide Receiver |url=http://www.elevenwarriors.com/ohio-state-football/2016/09/73791/cleveland-browns-name-terrelle-pryor-starting-wide-receiver |access-date=September 11, 2016 |website=ElevenWarriors.com |archive-date=September 9, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160909190944/http://www.elevenwarriors.com/ohio-state-football/2016/09/73791/cleveland-browns-name-terrelle-pryor-starting-wide-receiver |url-status=live }}</ref> (born June 20, 1989) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] and [[quarterback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). Considered the most recruited high school football-basketball athlete in southwestern [[Pennsylvania]] since [[Tom Clements]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=White |first=Mike |date=August 29, 2007 |title=Jeannette High School's two-sport superstar Terrelle Pryor |url=http://www.post-gazette.com/pg/07241/812755-365.stm |access-date=April 16, 2008 |website=Pittsburgh Post-Gazette |archive-date=May 3, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080503052654/http://www.post-gazette.com/pg/07241/812755-365.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> Pryor was widely regarded as the nation's top football prospect of 2008 and was named "Junior of the Year" by [[Rivals.com]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 6, 2007 |title=Rivals.com Junior of the Year Terrelle Pryor |url=https://n.rivals.com/news/video-rivals-com-junior-of-the-year-terrelle-pryor |access-date=April 27, 2023 |website=Rivals.com |archive-date=April 27, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230427030044/https://n.rivals.com/news/video-rivals-com-junior-of-the-year-terrelle-pryor |url-status=live }}</ref> Pryor had originally hoped to be a two-sport athlete, as he was also one of the nation's most recruited high school basketball players, but he later chose football.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Halley |first=Jim |date=December 26, 2007 |title=The 2007 All-USA players |url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/preps/football/2007-12-26-player-coach-of-the-year_N.htm?loc=interstitialskip |access-date=April 17, 2008 |website=USA Today |archive-date=February 14, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080214022931/http://www.usatoday.com/sports/preps/football/2007-12-26-player-coach-of-the-year_N.htm?loc=interstitialskip |url-status=live }}</ref>

A native of Florida, Cody spent two seasons at [[Mississippi Gulf Coast Community College]], where he helped the Bulldogs to an unbeaten season in 2007. Surprisingly nimble even at a peak weight of more than {{convert|400|lb|kg}}, Cody drew the attention of major [[Division I (NCAA)|Division I]] programs.  He finished his collegiate career at Alabama, where he earned consensus [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors twice while anchoring one of college football's best defenses during the [[2008 NCAA Division I FBS football season|2008]] and [[2009 NCAA Division I FBS football season|2009 season]]s.<ref name="ThamelNYT" /><ref name="Dufrense LATimes">{{Citation |title=Forget the statistics, Terrence Cody is a big deal for Alabama |url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/la-sp-dufresne-alabama4-2010jan04,0,3902513,full.column |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100107055907/http://www.latimes.com/sports/la-sp-dufresne-alabama4-2010jan04,0,3902513,full.column |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 7, 2010 |newspaper=Los Angeles Times |date=January 4, 2010 |last=Dufresne |first=Chris }}</ref>  During his senior season with the Alabama Crimson Tide in 2009, he helped lead the Tide to an undefeated 14–0 season including a victory in the [[2010 BCS National Championship Game]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Whiteside |first=Kelly |date=January 7, 2010 |title=Alabama sidesteps Texas' charge to emerge with BCS title |url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/college/football/2010-01-07-bcs-title-game_N.htm |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100110203127/http://www.usatoday.com/sports/college/football/2010-01-07-bcs-title-game_N.htm |archive-date=2010-01-10 |website=USA Today}}</ref>

Cody is one of the few football players ever to win a championship at Junior College, NCAA Division I College, and in the NFL.

'''Terrence Lamonte Warren''' (born August 2, 1969) is an American former professional [[gridiron football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) and [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL). After his stint in San Francisco, he signed with the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]], though he never played for the team due to injury. Warren was inducted into the Hampton University Athletics Hall of Fame on January 14, 2011, and the Central Intercollegiate Athletic (CIAA) Hall of Fame on February 27, 2015.
